title: Peas and carrots, canned, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Peas and carrots in cans are a ready‑to‑eat vegetable mix that has been blanched and sealed in oil. The product retains most of the flavor and nutrients of the fresh vegetables, while the added fat makes it more caloric and gives a creamy taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canning allows the vegetables to be stored for several years without quality loss.
Peas are a good source of plant protein, and carrots provide provitamin A (beta‑carotene).
The pea‑carrot combination is traditional in many cuisines as a nutritious side dish.
Adding fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as A and E.
Canned mixes are often used in baby foods and in diets where cooking facilities are limited.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peas contain about 5 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Carrots provide a high amount of beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A for eye health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: The vegetables retain some fiber, which aids normal digestion.

items.title: Fat enhances vitamin absorption
items.content: The added oil helps the body better absorb fat‑soluble vitamins A and E.

items.title: Low sodium when unsalted
items.content: Choosing a no‑salt version provides minerals without excess sodium.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Added oil increases the energy density, so portion size should be monitored.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergic reaction to peas.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Certain canned versions contain salt; people watching sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some products may contain additives; opt for preservative‑free versions if preferred.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The canned peas and carrots can be eaten cold in salads, added to soups, stews, or used as a side dish for meat and fish. They can also be gently warmed in a pan with a pinch of spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 3‑5 days, discarding if any off‑odors or signs of spoilage appear.
